A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniPR-3D, with readable text, equations, tables and figures. V1 includes Appendices A–F; v3 has no separate appendix. Retained content can be reliably matched across the formatting changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original single-frame and sequence-retrieval experiments, token ablations, and supplementary threshold and sequence-length evaluations.

after.justification: V3 reports original retrieval results and ablations, including retained sequence experiments and expanded single-frame comparisons.

M1.justification: The proposed VGGT backbone, five descriptor components, GeM/MLP and optimal-transport aggregation, anchor/support-frame processing, and training loss remain unchanged. RGB-only input clarification and the expanded aggregation/pose ablations do not establish a change to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: V3 adds Tokyo 24/7 and SF-XL v1, v2, night and occlusion evaluations, substantially broadening single-frame testing under illumination changes and occlusions. The original evaluation datasets and explicitly named training datasets, GSV-Cities and MSLS, remain.

E2.justification: Single-frame Table 1 adds AP-GeM, AnyLoc, CricaVPR, BoQ and MegaLoc, while removing the original GeM and Conv-AP comparisons. AP-GeM cites a different method from GeM. DINOv2 SALAD is retained as SALAD, and the main sequence-comparison membership remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 3.4 changes reported training precision from FP16 to float32. Single-frame Table 1 replaces R@5 with R@10 and adds a starred model using unspecified MegaLoc training settings. The broader appendix threshold and sequence-length evaluation grids are removed. These are reported setting/design changes, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Table 4 expands token ablations from Oxford2 to four datasets and adds explicit OT-versus-GeM patch aggregation and additional token combinations. Pose inclusion was already tested in v1. Conversely, v1's broader threshold/length sweeps and six supplementary retrieval figures disappear. The narrower Tables 3 and 5 remain, and the t-SNE analysis is relocated rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for its results. Both primarily report point-estimate recall values.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds extensive results and replaces existing scores: standard UniPR-3D MSLS Challenge R@1 changes from 74.3 to 75.5, for example. Changed reported settings prevent treating this as a controlled performance gain. Table 4 also replaces and expands results; additional appendix results and single-frame latency values disappear. Reported values in Tables 2, 3 and 5 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10 retain the same pooling, transport, assignment and descriptor formulations. Distinguishing 2D/3D register-token subscripts and changing patch notation are not substantive mathematical revisions. Neither version adds theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the first-effective-multiview-architecture claim to integration of geometry-aware information. The central contributions—3D-token VPR, tailored 2D/3D aggregation, variable-length sequence retrieval and state-of-the-art performance—remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: V3 explains viewpoint-reversed Oxford matches and interprets unsuccessful explicit pose injection as evidence that 3D tokens already encode sufficient spatial relationships. It explicitly clarifies RGB-only applicability without camera parameters. V1 Appendix C's qualification about unstable full fine-tuning is omitted; the main token-complementarity interpretation remains.

D1.justification: Removing Appendices B–C loses the exact 392×518 crop, Conv–ReLU–Conv and MLP implementation descriptions, and last-block-only fine-tuning disclosure. V3 adds RGB-only clarification and MLP/Fourier pose-projector details, but does not specify its aligned resolution or starred training configuration. Hardware, optimizer and learning-rate details remain; the future release promise additionally mentions datasets.

R1.justification: The cited literature expands substantially to additional VPR, 3D geometry and downstream-model work, including BoQ, AP-GeM, CricaVPR, SelaVPR++, DENS3R and MORE. Related work more explicitly positions novelty as fusion of single-view 2D and geometry-aware multiview tokens. These additions go beyond reference renumbering or publication-metadata updates.

P1.justification: The main section order and much of the prose remain intact. V3 makes localized rewrites and clarifications, integrates the retained t-SNE discussion into the main experiments, removes the separate supplementary sections, and adds an author, corresponding-author information and acknowledgements.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout, substantially resizing and relocating displays. Tables 1 and 4 are restructured, single-frame size/latency columns disappear, appendix Tables 6–7 and Figures 5–10 are removed, and a viewpoint-reversal illustration is added. V1 Figure 11's t-SNE plot becomes v3 Figure 6.

improvement.justification: Expanded single-frame benchmarks, stronger comparator coverage and broader aggregation ablations improve validation. However, v3 loses cross-dataset threshold/length evidence supporting its central generalization claims, concrete implementation details and single-frame efficiency reporting. The new training configuration is also incompletely specified. These material gains and losses leave the overall quality direction uncertain.
